attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article, not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Severely doubt' is graded doubt, not a firm assertion, and 'very unlikely' captures that. The drafter's 'past six months' adds an anchor the source lacks ('in the space of six months'), but this doesn't change the result.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to turn doubt into certainty or to choose a profit measure the speaker never named (inference, gross, or operating).

reviews.rationale: The statement expresses strong personal doubt, which is graded confidence and not a firm claim. It also never defines which profitability measure is meant, and the six-month window has no endpoint. Under the policy, hedged or probabilistic language is not scored. The packet contains no evidence items.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. He bases it on the SpaceX S-1 but states it himself.

semantics.note: 'Will start paying' in July is an unhedged forecast. The monthly amount, the annualised figure and the 'on top of' other deals are all preserved.

contract.note: A plain reading (the full monthly charge starts in July 2026, with the other deals kept) is fair and ordinary. It is reasonable to require evidence that goes beyond repeating the contract schedule.

evidence.note: WIRED, May 20: confirms the contracted schedule (reduced fee May–June, then $1.25B a month). It predates July, so it shows the plan was agreed, not that it was carried out.

Stocktwits, Oct 2: says the full rate has applied since July. But it is framed around the May filing and cites no invoice or new source, so it reads as a restatement of the schedule. It is also silent on whether the other compute deals were kept.

reviews.rationale: The July 2026 deadline has passed. e1 shows only the agreed schedule. e2 asserts the full rate applied from July, but it seems to restate the May filing rather than give independent confirmation, which the contract excludes. Nothing in the packet confirms July charges or that the other compute deals continued. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the forecast either way.
